footer: Photographs made for this edition, in the same light throughout. The wording follows the cards. Where a margin note changed the dish, that is the version written here.

recipes.title: Swedish Pancakes
recipes.intro: Thin, tender, and better if you wait. The batter wants a long rest — overnight if you can.

items: Melt the butter and cool it slightly.
With an electric beater, beat the eggs and salt.
Add the milk and cream. Add the flour. Add the melted butter. Beat thoroughly for 2 minutes.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and chill for at least 1 hour, but preferably overnight.

To cook, heat the pan and lightly grease with shortening. Beat the pancake mix slightly to blend. Pour about ½ cup of mix into the pan and cook on medium heat until golden brown. Flip and cook the other side.

notes.label: From the card
notes.text: For crispy pancakes, use a cast iron pan.

recipes.title: Jiffy Cinnamon Buns
recipes.intro: Biscuit dough, brown-sugar butter, baked in muffin tins. Flip them out the moment they come from the oven.

items: Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. Blend in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse meal.
Pour in the milk, stirring lightly. Turn onto a floured surface and knead 8–10 times. Roll into a 12 × 8-inch rectangle.
Cream the butter, brown sugar, and cinnamon. Spread over the dough. Sprinkle with raisins.
Roll up jelly-roll style from the long side, seam under. Cut into 12 pieces. Place in greased muffin tins.
Bake at 400°F for 20 minutes. Watch the time — check after 15 minutes. Flip out immediately.

notes.label: From the card
notes.text: Roll out like a log, then seam under.

notes.label: The usual way
notes.text: I usually take them out after 15 minutes.

recipes.title: Peanut Chicken Stir Fry
recipes.intro: Broiled chicken, a pan of steamed vegetables, rice cooked in broth — and the peanut-hoisin sauce served on the side, to drizzle.

ingredients.label: Chicken & rice
items: Chicken breasts, sliced into thin strips

ingredients.label: Sauce
items: Water, to thin if the sauce becomes too thick
Slice the chicken breasts into thin strips. Place in a bowl and toss with a little olive oil for at least 10 minutes. Place the chicken on a foil-lined sheet and season with salt and pepper.
Wash and cook the rice in chicken broth.
In a pot, mix the sauce — broth, peanut butter, hoisin, cider vinegar, and garlic — and simmer. Thin with water if it becomes too thick.
Turn the broiler to high and move the rack to the second rung.
Wash and thinly slice the broccoli, celery, carrots, and red pepper.
Grill the chicken 6 minutes on one side. Flip and grill 6 minutes on the second side.
Cook the red peppers in hot oil in an electric fry pan. Then add the broccoli, carrots, and celery. Put on the lid. Add a little, little water (not much) to steam.
Put the rice on a large platter. Top with the vegetables and chicken.
Put the sauce in a separate bowl to drizzle over the vegetables and chicken.

notes.label: From the card
notes.text: A little, little water — not much — to steam. Sauce stays on the side, for drizzling.

recipes.title: Super Salmon Loaf
recipes.intro: A mid-century loaf, baked in a water bath and turned out onto a warm platter. The clipping called for parsley. The card says dill.

items: 2 tablespoons chopped dill (the clipping said parsley)

Drain the salmon juices into a medium saucepan. Add the butter and milk to the salmon juice and heat just until the butter melts. Remove from heat; stir in the cracker crumbs and let stand five minutes.

Flake the salmon and fold into the crumb mixture along with the well-mashed bones. Beat the egg yolks and fold into the salmon mixture along with the remaining ingredients except the egg whites. Beat the egg whites until they form soft peaks. Fold into the salmon mixture.

Grease an 8½ × 4½-inch loaf pan and line with wax paper, leaving about an inch of paper to form a collar around the edges of the pan. Grease the paper. Pour the salmon mixture into the prepared pan and set in a shallow baking pan. Pour boiling water into the baking pan to a depth of one inch.
Bake in a moderate oven, 350°F, for 45 to 55 minutes. Remove the pan from the water. Let stand for five minutes before unmoulding onto a heated platter. Garnish with lemon slices.

notes.label: Written in the margin
notes.text: Dill — not parsley.

recipes.title: Lettuce Wraps
recipes.intro: Minced chicken or pork, a hoisin-oyster sauce, and whole lettuce leaves washed the day before. Roll them at the table.
details: Lettuce washed and chilled the day before

ingredients.label: Filling
items: A chunk of fresh ginger, minced
Prepare all the ingredients and the sauce ahead of cooking.
Have whole lettuce leaves washed and chilled the day before. When washing, separate each leaf individually.
Mince the garlic, green onions, red pepper, ginger, carrot, and water chestnuts.
Make the sauce by combining the hoisin, oyster sauce, sesame oil, and sugar in a bowl. Stir to mix.
Heat olive oil in a fry pan over medium heat. Gently cook the garlic, onions, red pepper, ginger, carrot, and water chestnuts.

Add 1 pound of minced chicken or pork. Stir to break it up and cook until cooked through. Season with salt and pepper. Add the sauce to the meat mixture. Just before serving, add a handful of steamed noodles.
Spoon into lettuce cups. Drizzle with hoisin. Eat and roll up.

notes.label: The day before
notes.text: Wash and chill the leaves. Separate each one.

notes.label: In the margin
notes.text: Hoisin is 3 tablespoons, with “¾ cup + 1 Tbsp” written beside it.

recipes.title: Oriental Meatballs
recipes.intro: Gingersnap meatballs baked, then finished in a ketchup and pineapple sauce. The clipping says soy sauce twice. The margin says to add it carefully, in the sauce.
details: 10 minutes, then 10–15 more in the sauce

ingredients.label: Meatballs
items: 1 (398 mL) can crushed pineapple, drained well, syrup reserved

method.label: Meatballs
items: Combine the beef, gingersnap crumbs, egg, soy sauce, crushed pineapple, salt, mustard, pepper, and garlic powder.
Form into 24 meatballs, about 1½ inches across. Place in a shallow baking pan.

method.label: Sauce
items: Combine the ketchup, soy sauce, ginger, mustard, brown sugar, and pineapple syrup.
Pour over the meatballs and continue baking 10 to 15 minutes longer.

notes.label: Written beside the soy sauce
notes.text: Add the soy sauce carefully, in the sauce portion.

notes.label: In the margin
notes.text: Add honey to the sauce. Garlic. Use cookie crumb — blend till very fine.

recipes.title: Smack Cake
recipes.intro: A crumbly butter base and a coconut meringue top. The card is very clear about the coconut: stir, do not beat.

method.label: Base
items: Lightly grease an 8 × 8 baking pan, or line it with foil for easy removal.
Mix together the egg yolks and vanilla.
Combine the dry ingredients, egg, and melted butter to form a crumbly mixture.
Pat the mixture fairly firmly into the prepared pan.

method.label: Topping
items: Beat the egg whites until they are stiff.
Add the salt and sugar and beat again.
Stir in (very important to stir, not beat) the coconut.
Gently spread the topping onto the base layer.

notes.label: Very important
notes.text: Stir in the coconut — do not beat.

recipes.title: Chocolate Cake
recipes.intro: A two-layer cocoa cake, sifted straight into the mixer bowl and beaten in two short rounds — one minute, then two.

items: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Grease two 9-inch round layer cake pans and line the bottoms with wax paper.
Sift the flour, cocoa, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and granulated sugar together into a large mixer bowl.
Add the shortening, brown sugar, 1 cup of the milk, and the vanilla. Beat for 1 minute at low speed of an electric mixer, or 150 strokes by hand.
Add the remaining ¼ cup milk and the eggs. Beat for 2 minutes at low speed.
Pour the batter into the prepared pans. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, or until the cake springs back when lightly touched.
Cool 5 minutes, then remove from the pans.

notes.label: From the page
notes.text: No mixer? 150 strokes by hand does the same job.

notes.label: Done when
notes.text: The cake springs back when lightly touched.

recipes.title: Banana Cake
recipes.intro: Ripe bananas and buttermilk, added alternately with the flour. Two 8-inch layers, from page 124.

items: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Grease two 8-inch round layer cake pans and line the bottoms with wax paper.
Sift together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
Cream the shortening. Beat in the sugar, then blend in the eggs and vanilla, beating until light and fluffy.
Add the dry ingredients to the creamed mixture alternately with the bananas and buttermilk — 3 dry and 2 liquid additions, combining lightly after each.
Turn into the prepared pans. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, or until the cake springs back when lightly touched.
Cool 5 minutes, then remove from the pans.

notes.label: From the page
notes.text: Three dry, two liquid — combine lightly after each.

recipes.title: Jelly Roll
recipes.intro: A quick sponge baked thin, turned out onto a sugared towel and rolled while warm. Then fill it with jam, jelly, or filling.

method.label: Sponge
items: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Grease a 15 × 10 × 1-inch jelly roll pan and line it with wax paper.
Sift together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
Beat the eggs, sugar, and lemon juice until thick and lemon-coloured. Gradually beat in the hot milk, and keep beating until very thick.
Sift the dry ingredients over the egg mixture in four portions, folding gently after each.
Turn into the prepared pan. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, or until the cake springs back when lightly touched.

method.label: Rolling
items: Turn out immediately onto a towel sprinkled with icing sugar.
Peel off the wax paper and roll the cake up, rolling the towel up inside it. Let it cool.
Unroll, fill with jam, jelly, or filling, and re-roll.

notes.label: Don't wait
notes.text: Turn it out the moment it leaves the oven, and roll it up in the towel while warm.

recipes.title: Apple Streusel Cake
recipes.intro: A German Apfelstreuselkuchen: a lemony butter sponge, a ring of tart apple slices, and a cold cinnamon crumble on top. Serve warm or cold, with whipped cream.

ingredients.label: Dry
items: 1¼ cups (150 g) flour — UK plain, US all-purpose, German type 405
⅓ cup (50 g) corn flour / cornstarch

ingredients.label: Apples
items: 4 tart apples, about 1 kg / 2 lb — Cox, Braeburn, or Granny Smith

ingredients.label: Batter
items: ½ cup (100 g) butter, at room temperature

ingredients.label: Cinnamon streusel
items: ½ cup (100 g) butter, at room temperature
2 tsp vanilla sugar (or 1 tsp vanilla extract)

method.label: Prepare
items: Grease the sides of the springform with butter and line the base with baking parchment. Preheat the oven to 180°C / 356°F, top and bottom heat.
Sift the flour, corn flour, baking powder, and salt into a bowl and set aside.
Peel, core, and slice the apples. Toss them in the lemon juice so they don’t brown.
For the streusel, combine the sugar, vanilla sugar, cinnamon, and butter in a medium bowl. Stir in the flour with a rubber spatula until thick and crumbly. Chill until needed.

method.label: Assemble and bake
items: Beat the butter and sugar at high speed until smooth and creamy, about 2 minutes. Add the eggs and mix for a further minute, then the lemon zest. Add the flour mixture and mix on low until just combined.
Spread the batter evenly in the tin.
Arrange the apple slices in circles over the batter.
Take the streusel from the fridge and crumble it over the cake with your fingers.
Bake for 35 to 45 minutes, until a skewer pushed into the middle comes out clean.
Keep at room temperature until serving. Dust with icing sugar if you like.

notes.label: From the recipe
notes.text: Use tart apples — Cox, Braeburn, or Granny Smith.

notes.label: Slice thickness
notes.text: Cut the apples about ¼ inch (5–6 mm) thick, thin enough to soften fully in the oven but thick enough to hold their shape.

notes.label: Keep it cold
notes.text: Chill the streusel until the last moment, then crumble it on by hand.

notes.label: To serve
notes.text: Warm or cold, with a dollop of freshly whipped cream.

recipes.title: Raspberry Ripple Cheesecake
recipes.intro: No oven needed: a buttery graham cracker base, a whipped cream-cheese filling, and a homemade raspberry purée swirled and feathered on top.

method.label: Base
items: Put the crackers in a bag and roll with a rolling pin to make crumbs.
Melt the butter in a pan. Pour in the crushed graham crackers and stir thoroughly.
Line an 8-inch (20 cm) cake pan with a removable base with plastic wrap. Spoon in the cracker mixture, press flat with a masher, and refrigerate.

method.label: Purée
items: Bring the raspberries and powdered sugar to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes. Cool, then press through a sieve.

method.label: Filling
items: Mix together the cream cheese, superfine sugar, and vanilla. Whip the cream until stiff, then fold it into the cheese mixture.
Spread about ¾ of the cheese mixture over the cracker base. Spoon on ¾ of the purée and swirl it into the cheesecake mixture.
Gently spread on the remaining cheesecake mixture. Drizzle straight lines of the remaining purée across the top and pull a skewer across the lines for a feathered effect.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.

notes.label: From the page
notes.text: Pull a skewer across the lines for a feathered effect.

notes.label: Grown-up help
notes.text: The book marks melting the butter and making the purée as hot steps.

recipes.title: Lemon Coconut Cake
recipes.intro: Written out in green pencil, with a drawing at the top. Coconut milk and coconut oil, brightened with lemon.

items: Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a cake pan.
Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder, and lemon zest in a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the eggs with the coconut milk, coconut oil, and lemon juice.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry until just combined, and pour into the pan.

notes.label: On the card
notes.text: 350° — 60 minutes.

notes.label: Good to know
notes.text: The card lists ingredients only, with no method or pan size. The steps here simply put them together.

recipes.title: Blueberry Pancakes
recipes.intro: Thick, fluffy pancakes with the blueberries dropped in as they cook. Cinnamon and maple flavouring to taste.

items: Beat the eggs. Beat in the milk, vegetable oil, and maple flavouring.
Add the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon to the liquid.
Heat the pan to high and grease lightly with shortening. Use about ½ cup batter for each pancake.
Drop blueberries into each pancake as the first side cooks. Once the first side is golden, flip and cook the second side.

notes.label: From the card
notes.text: If using frozen blueberries, cook a little longer to make sure the blueberries are thawed.

recipes.title: Roasted Pumpkin Coconut Curry Soup
recipes.intro: Everything roasts in one pot, then simmers with broth and coconut milk. The margins make it milder and creamier: one teaspoon of curry paste and a full can of coconut milk.

ingredients.label: To roast
items: 1 medium apple, cored and roughly chopped — don’t peel
1 large potato, roughly chopped — don’t peel
3 + 3 medium cloves garlic (the printout lists garlic twice)

ingredients.label: To finish
items: 1⅞ cups (30 tbsp) pumpkin purée — one 15-ounce can
One full 400 ml can light coconut milk

ingredients.label: Garnish
items: Greek yogurt thinned with a bit of milk, if desired

Combine the olive oil, butter, onion, apple, potato, garlic, curry paste, brown sugar, curry powder, coriander, cumin, and ginger in a Dutch oven or oven-safe pot. Stir well and roast in the preheated oven. (The roasting time is cut off on our copy.)
Remove from the oven and stir in the pumpkin purée. Roast for another 15–20 minutes, until deepening in colour, stirring halfway through.
Remove from the oven and add the chicken broth and coconut milk. Bring to a low simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
Cool first, then purée with an immersion blender or a regular blender. Reheat.
Serve with a small dollop of cream or Greek yogurt, a little coconut, some chopped cilantro, and a sprinkle of roughly chopped cashews.

notes.label: Written beside the curry paste
notes.text: Only 1 full tsp. The printout says 1–4 teaspoons, and 2 is medium spicy.

notes.label: In the margin
notes.text: Apple and potato — don’t peel. Pumpkin purée: 1.875 cups, 30 tbsp. Coconut milk: a full 400 ml can, not the 14½-ounce can printed.

notes.label: At the bottom
notes.text: Cool first, then blend — reheat. Garnish coconut.

recipes.attribution: Printed recipe by Chris Scheuer, with handwritten notes

recipes.title: Waffles
recipes.intro: The same simple batter family as the pancakes, with melted butter. Bake until the iron stops steaming.

items: Beat the eggs. Beat in the milk and melted butter.
Add the rest of the ingredients and beat just until smooth.
Heat the waffle iron. Pour in about ¾ to 1 cup of batter.
Bake until the waffle stops steaming.

notes.label: From the card
notes.text: Bake until the waffle stops steaming.

recipes.title: Camp Squeah Munch Bars
recipes.intro: Oats, Rice Krispies, coconut, and sunflower seeds, bound with melted marshmallows and finished with chocolate chips. A camp recipe, made by the potful.

items: Combine the rolled oats, Rice Krispies, coconut, and sunflower seeds in a large bowl.
In a large pot, melt the margarine. Add the marshmallows and stir.

notes.label: Good to know
notes.text: The newsletter stops at the chocolate chips. It gives no pan size or setting time.

recipes.title: Michelin Cottage Pie
recipes.intro: Short rib and shin instead of mince, braised low and slow for a rich, collagen-thick sauce, under a piped dome of duchesse potato. Inspired by John Williams's version at The Ritz.

ingredients.label: Beef braise
items: 450 g short rib, off the bone
450 g beef shin, off the bone
Bouquet garni: the dark green end of a leek wrapped around thyme, rosemary, and bay

ingredients.label: To finish
items: Clarified or melted butter, for brushing

method.label: Braise the beef
items: Heat the oven to 150°C / 300°F. Season the short rib and shin with fine salt. Heat the olive oil over medium-high heat and brown the meat all over until dark golden brown. Lift out the meat.
Pour the red wine into the pan and reduce by two-thirds, or until it starts to taste sweet.
Return the meat with the reduced wine, beef stock, and bouquet garni. Cover with a cartouche and a lid, and braise in the oven for 2½ hours.

method.label: Bake the potatoes
items: Heat the oven to 180°C / 350°F. Prick the potatoes and bake them whole on a bed of salt for 40 minutes, or until completely soft — larger potatoes can take about an hour.

method.label: Sauté the vegetables
items: Melt 10 g of the butter until foaming. Over medium-high heat, sauté the mushrooms for 4–5 minutes until softened and golden. Set aside.
Add another 10 g butter, turn the heat to medium, and sauté the shallots for 4–5 minutes until soft and starting to turn golden.

Add the last 10 g butter and the carrots. Sauté over medium heat for 4–5 minutes until starting to soften and colour. Stir in the tomato purée and cook it out for a couple of minutes. Combine all the vegetables and set aside.

method.label: Finish the filling
items: After 2½ hours, pick out the bouquet garni. Pull the meat apart into chunks, add the carrots, shallots, and mushrooms, cover again with the cartouche and lid, and return to the oven for 30 minutes.
Season, then leave to cool — over ice, if you like.

method.label: Duchesse potatoes
items: While the potatoes are still warm, scoop out the insides and push them through a fine drum sieve (a ricer, then a sieve, works too).
Gently fold in the melted butter and egg yolks until smooth. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg to taste.

method.label: Assemble and bake
items: Fill a small pie or casserole dish with the cooled filling, leaving about an inch at the top for the potato.
Pipe the duchesse potato over the top, starting at the edge and working inward to a generous dome. Smooth it and mark ridges with a palette knife or fork. Leave to cool.
Brush the top with clarified butter and bake at 180°C / 350°F for 30 minutes, until golden.

notes.label: From the video
notes.text: Reduce the wine on its own first, until the tannins are gone and it tastes sweet. Added straight in, it tastes winey.

notes.label: Bake, don't boil
notes.text: Boiled potatoes make watery mash. Baking them whole on salt dries them out, so the duchesse holds its shape and browns.

notes.label: Keep it firm
notes.text: Fold gently and keep the potato stiff. Too soft or too much fat and it foams in the oven and turns spongy. Pipe onto a cooled filling.

recipes.title: Chicken Tetrazzini
recipes.intro: Spaghetti and chicken in a creamy three-part sauce, with mushrooms, pimientos, and Parmesan. One batch fills two dishes: one for tonight, one for the freezer or a friend.

ingredients.label: Filling
items: 3 cans (4 ounces each) mushroom stems and pieces, drained

method.label: Sauce and pasta
items: Cook the spaghetti until al dente, according to the package directions. Drain and set aside.
In a Dutch oven, melt the butter. Stir in the flour, salt, and pepper until smooth. Gradually whisk in the broth, half-and-half, and whipping cream.
Bring to a boil, then cook and stir until thickened, about 2 minutes.
Remove from the heat. Stir in the chicken, mushrooms, pimientos, and spaghetti, tossing gently to coat.

method.label: Bake one
items: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Divide the mixture between two greased 11 × 7-inch baking dishes and sprinkle with Parmesan.
Bake one casserole, uncovered, until heated through, 20 to 25 minutes.

method.label: Freeze one
items: Cover and freeze the second casserole for up to 2 months.
To serve, thaw in the refrigerator overnight. Cover and bake at 350° for 30 minutes, then uncover and bake until heated through, 15 to 20 minutes more. Stir before serving.

notes.label: From the recipe
notes.text: Cook the spaghetti only to al dente. It soaks up sauce in the oven without going mushy.

notes.label: For the freezer
notes.text: Up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge, then bake covered first.

notes.label: Before serving
notes.text: Give the reheated casserole a stir.

recipes.title: Honey Mustard Sauce
recipes.intro: Sweet, tangy, and creamy, stirred together in five minutes from things already in the fridge. Mayonnaise and sour cream for body, two mustards for bite. Made for chicken fingers, fries, and roasted broccoli.

items: 2 tablespoons mayonnaise — homemade if you have it
1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice or distilled white vinegar
Put the mayonnaise, sour cream, honey, both mustards, and the lemon juice or vinegar in a medium bowl.
Stir until smooth and evenly blended.
Taste. Add a little more honey for a sweeter sauce, or more mustard for more bite.
Spoon into a jar or airtight container and keep in the refrigerator for up to two weeks.

notes.label: From the recipe
notes.text: Use both mustards: yellow brings the vinegary tang, Dijon the punch.

notes.label: Taste as you go
notes.text: Honeys vary in sweetness, so adjust the honey to suit.

notes.label: To serve
notes.text: Dip chicken nuggets, fish sticks, or fries, or spoon over pork chops, grilled chicken, and roasted broccoli.

notes.label: Keeps
notes.text: Up to two weeks, covered, in the fridge.

recipes.title: Spaetzle
recipes.intro: Little German egg dumplings, somewhere between a noodle and a dumpling, with a whisper of nutmeg. Just flour, eggs, milk, and salt, pressed straight into boiling water. Toss with butter, or crisp them in a hot pan the way it's done in Germany.
details: 2–3 minutes per batch, in boiling water

method.label: Make the dough
items: In a medium to large bowl, stir together the flour, salt, and nutmeg.
In a second bowl, beat the eggs in one at a time until well blended, then whisk in the milk.
Make a well in the center of the flour and pour in the egg mixture. Stir until a soft dough forms: thicker than a batter, spoonable but not pourable.
Cover the bowl with a tea towel and let the dough rest for about 10 minutes.

method.label: Cook
items: Bring 2 to 3 quarts of lightly salted water to a boil.
Spoon about half the dough into a spaetzle maker, or onto a grater, colander, or steamer basket held over the pot, and push it through the holes with a spatula, letting it drop into the water.
Stir gently. Cook 2 to 3 minutes, until the dumplings float to the top.
Lift them out with a slotted spoon, drain in a colander, and turn into a bowl. Repeat with the rest of the dough.
Toss with butter and serve warm, or brown them in melted butter in a large hot frying pan, turning once, until crisp on both sides.

notes.label: No spaetzle maker?
notes.text: Press the dough through the large holes of a box grater, a colander, or a steamer basket with a spatula.

notes.label: The dough
notes.text: Aim for just thicker than batter: it should hold on a spoon but not pour.

notes.label: To serve
notes.text: Buttered, or pan-fried until crisp, with a sprinkle of chopped parsley.

notes.label: Bacon and onion
notes.text: Fry finely diced bacon and onion for a couple of minutes before adding the spaetzle to the pan.

notes.label: Käsespätzle
notes.text: Layer the warm spaetzle in a baking dish with shredded Swiss cheese between the layers, top with bacon and sautéed onions, and bake at 375°F for about 12 minutes.

notes.label: Keeps
notes.text: Several days, covered, in the fridge. Rewarm briefly in boiling water, or in the microwave with a splash of water and a little butter. Freezes for 3 to 4 months; thaw overnight in the fridge.

recipes.title: Ground Beef Stroganoff
recipes.intro: All the comfort of a classic stroganoff, with none of the gamble on a pricey steak. Browned mince, golden onions, and button mushrooms simmered in a mustardy beef gravy, finished off the heat with sour cream. One skillet, no oven, and supper on the table in about half an hour.
details: Serve over buttered pasta, egg noodles, rice, or mash

items: 1 lb (450 g) ground beef, preferably 10% fat or leaner
⅔ cup (150 ml) sour cream or crème fraîche
Pasta, egg noodles, rice, or mashed potatoes, to serve

method.label: Brown the beef
items: Heat a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef, break it into small lumps with a spatula, and cook for about 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until browned.
Stir in the onion and garlic and season with the salt and pepper. Turn the heat to medium and cook for another 3–4 minutes, until the onion is soft and starting to caramelize.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 4–5 minutes, until softened.

method.label: Make the sauce
items: Push the beef out toward the edges of the pan to clear a small space in the middle. Melt 1 tablespoon of the butter there, stir in the flour, and cook for a minute to make a smooth paste.
Add the Worcestershire sauce and Dijon mustard and stir everything together with the beef.
Pour in the beef stock, stirring gently so the flour dissolves. Simmer for 2–3 minutes, until the sauce thickens slightly.

method.label: Finish
items: Meanwhile, cook your pasta in well-salted water for a minute less than the packet says, drain, and toss with the remaining 1 tablespoon butter.
Turn off the heat under the stroganoff and stir in the sour cream until the sauce is creamy. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Spoon over the buttered pasta and scatter with parsley.

notes.label: Off the heat
notes.text: Stir the sour cream in once the pan is off the heat so it stays smooth and doesn't split.

notes.label: Lean mince
notes.text: Choose mince with no more than 10% fat so the sauce isn't greasy. Pork, turkey, chicken, or lamb all work too.

notes.label: More traditional
notes.text: Add a good teaspoon of paprika along with the salt and pepper.

notes.label: Swaps
notes.text: Soy sauce or balsamic vinegar can stand in for Worcestershire; chicken or vegetable stock works in place of beef; cornflour or rice flour makes it gluten-free.

notes.label: Keeps
notes.text: Up to 3 days in the fridge. Reheat gently over medium-low heat.

recipes.title: Earl Grey Scones
recipes.intro: Tender, golden wedges with the gentle bergamot of Earl Grey steeped right into the milk. Lovely warm from the oven with butter and a spoonful of apricot jam.
recipes.image_alt: Earl Grey scones with apricot jam and a cup of tea

method.label: Steep the tea
items: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and lightly grease a baking sheet.
Bring the milk to a simmer in a small pot, then take it off the heat. Add the tea bags and let them steep for 30 minutes before lifting them out.

method.label: Make the dough
items: In a large bowl, combine the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt. Cut in the butter.
In a small bowl, mix the beaten egg with the tea-infused milk, then stir it into the flour mixture.

method.label: Shape and bake
items: Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead briefly.
Roll it into a ½-inch (1.3 cm) thick round and cut into 8 wedges.
Place on the prepared sheet and bake for 15 minutes, until golden brown.

notes.label: Give it time
notes.text: Let the tea steep the full 30 minutes; that's where all the flavour comes from.

notes.label: To serve
notes.text: Warm, with apricot jam, as pictured on the card.

recipes.title: German Pancake
recipes.intro: Six simple ingredients whisked in five minutes, poured over sizzling butter, and baked until the edges puff up tall and golden. A cherished family breakfast that brings everyone running to the table.
recipes.image_alt: German pancake with powdered sugar, strawberries and syrup

items: Whisk together the eggs, milk, flour, salt and vanilla until smooth.
Put the butter in a 9 × 13-inch metal baking dish and set it in the oven while it preheats to 425°F (218°C), so the butter melts.
Pour the batter over the hot melted butter.
Bake for 22 to 27 minutes, until the edges are puffed up and beautifully golden brown.
Dust generously with powdered sugar, drizzle with syrup, and serve right away.

notes.label: Watch it rise
notes.text: It puffs dramatically in the oven and settles as it cools, so bring it straight to the table.

notes.label: To serve
notes.text: Fresh strawberries are lovely alongside, as in the original post.

recipes.title: Naan Bread
recipes.intro: Soft, pillowy flatbreads that puff and blister in a hot pan in about a minute a side. Six pantry ingredients and a short rest, then serve them plain or brushed with garlic and fresh herbs alongside any curry.
recipes.image_alt: Stack of garlic and herb naan bread on a wooden board

ingredients.label: For cooking
items: Extra flour, if the dough is sticky and for rolling
A little olive oil for the pan

method.label: Make the dough
items: Stir the warm water, sugar and yeast together in a bowl (or a stand mixer) and leave for about 5 minutes, until foamy.
Add the flour and salt and mix for about 30 seconds.
Add the olive oil and keep kneading for about 5 minutes, until it forms a firm dough ball. If it's sticky, add a little more flour.
Cover the bowl and leave it somewhere warm to rest for about 30 minutes.

method.label: Shape and cook
items: Divide the dough into small balls.
On a floured surface, roll each one out into a rough round, or stretch it by hand.
Heat a griddle or frying pan, add a little olive oil and wipe it around with a paper towel.
Cook each naan about 1 minute per side, until it puffs up and has brown spots on both sides.

notes.label: Garlic naan
notes.text: The video shows a garlic version topped with garlic and fresh herbs, but doesn't give amounts or say when they go on. Brushing the hot naan with garlic butter and scattering herbs over it works well.

notes.label: No rolling pin?
notes.text: Stretching the dough by hand works just as well.

recipes.title: Roberta's Pizza Dough
recipes.intro: The famous Brooklyn pizzeria's dough: a mix of silky 00 and chewy bread flour, just a pinch of yeast, and a slow rise. It's ready in a few hours, but even better after a day in the fridge.
recipes.image_alt: Two balls of pizza dough and a stretched round on a floured board

items: Stir the yeast into the warm water and let it sit for a few minutes.
Whisk the two flours and the salt together in a large bowl.
Add the yeast water and olive oil and mix until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead on a lightly floured surface until smooth and elastic, about 3 minutes.
Let rest 15 minutes, then knead briefly again.
Divide into 2 balls, cover, and let rise 3 to 4 hours at room temperature, or 18 to 24 hours in the fridge.
Stretch each ball into a round, top as you like, and bake in a very hot oven.

notes.label: From the chart
notes.text: The chart gives only the ingredients, the rising time and the yield. The steps above are the usual method for this dough.

notes.label: Slow rise
notes.text: The 18–24 hour fridge rise gives the most flavour. Let the dough come to room temperature before you stretch it.

recipes.attribution: Roberta's, via a Pizza Dough Showdown chart

recipes.title: Chicken Pesto Lasagna
recipes.intro: A creamy white lasagna that skips the red sauce. Ground chicken, a garlicky ricotta and pesto filling, and roasted garlic parmesan sauce are layered three times under a golden, herb-flecked blanket of mozzarella.
recipes.image_alt: Chicken pesto lasagna with a golden cheese top in a glass dish

ingredients.label: To assemble
items: 1 jar store-bought roasted garlic and parmesan sauce (or your own white sauce)

method.label: Make the filling
items: Cook the ground chicken in a pan and set it aside.
In a bowl, mix the ricotta, a handful of mozzarella, the parmesan, garlic, pesto and eggs until combined.

method.label: Layer and bake
items: Spread a thin layer of sauce over the bottom of a square baking dish and add a layer of no-boil noodles.
Spread on some of the ricotta mixture, then a generous layer of mozzarella and some of the chicken. Drizzle with a little sauce.
Repeat the noodles, ricotta, mozzarella, chicken and sauce layers twice more, for three layers in all. Go easy on the sauce so it lasts.
Finish with a layer of noodles, a thick covering of mozzarella and a sprinkle of Italian seasoning.
Bake at 375°F for 25 minutes, until bubbly and golden.

notes.label: About the amounts
notes.text: The video doesn't give measurements, only one clove of garlic, two eggs and two noodles per layer. Use enough to fill your dish.

notes.label: Sauce swap
notes.text: Your own favourite white sauce works in place of the jar.
